title: pbeesly multi-stage PowerShell credential/secret collection toolkit on scranton
rationale: F02 describes the surrounding pbeesly attack toolkit (Invoke-Discovery, Invoke-Persistence, Get-PrivateKeys, Invoke-Exfil, Invoke-SeaDukeStage, Keystroke-Check, Invoke-ScreenCapture) on scranton; the credential-access component is general OS Credential Dumping (T1003).

title: LSASS memory access with full-access masks by attacker PowerShell/wsmprovhost on scranton and nashua
rationale: All six findings describe the same attacker action: PowerShell.exe (PID 2976, pbeesly/SYSTEM) and wsmprovhost.exe opening lsass.exe with GrantedAccess 0x1FFFFF/0x1F3FFF on scranton and nashua on 2020-05-02. F32 and F34/F45 add the DPAPI/Credential Manager and steganographic-loader context but the observed action is the same LSASS handle acquisition, which best fits OS Credential Dumping: LSASS Memory (T1003.001).

title: lsass.exe creates PASSWD.LOG and opens SAM hive with KEY_ALL_ACCESS on scranton
rationale: F60 and F61 describe the same SAM credential-dump sequence on scranton: lsass.exe creating C:\Windows\debug\PASSWD.LOG at 03:19:09 followed by lsass.exe opening the SAM registry object with AccessMask 0xf003f (KEY_ALL_ACCESS) at 03:19:21-03:20:46, matching Security Account Manager (T1003.002).

title: Reflective in-memory API resolution and shellcode loader via PowerShell on scranton
rationale: F08, F21 and F52 all describe the same PowerShell 4104 script block (ScriptBlockId bc19aae2-d1f9-49b2-b718-192531ae928f, user pbeesly) resolving GetProcAddress/GetModuleHandle, building a ReflectedDelegate dynamic assembly and decoding base64 shellcode. F52 explicitly notes no SAML/token forging was observed, so the in-scope technique best matching the observed API-hooking/reflective-loading behavior is Credential API Hooking (T1056.004).

title: WebDAV/SMB forced-authentication coercion from scranton to 192.168.0.4
rationale: F19 describes scranton (10.0.1.4) connecting to 192.168.0.4 over SMB and issuing WebDAV PROPFIND/OPTIONS requests carrying an AUTHORIZATION header, the forced-authentication coercion pattern matching T1187.

title: accesschk.exe run by pbeesly creating a 'passwordsDB' file on scranton
rationale: F28 describes pbeesly launching accesschk.exe (parent powershell.exe) which created C:\Program Files\SysinternalsSuite\passwordsDB, consistent with searching for credentials stored in files (T1552.001).

title: Sysinternals pspasswd.exe/pspasswd64.exe downloaded to Downloads on scranton
rationale: F58 describes PowerShell (pbeesly) writing pspasswd.exe and pspasswd64.exe into Downloads\SysinternalsSuite, credential/password-manipulation tooling staged for credential collection, consistent with T1552.001.

title: Rar.exe on nashua creates password-protected working.zip then sdelete64 wipes it
rationale: F62 describes pbeesly launching Rar.exe on nashua to create a password-protected archive working.zip (password fGzq5yKw) followed by sdelete64.exe wiping Rar.exe and both archive copies; password-protected staging plus anti-forensic cleanup is consistent with credential/data collection in files (T1552.001).

title: Invoke-Exfil compresses Downloads with password 'lolol' and exfiltrates to WebDAV with hardcoded creds
rationale: F63 describes pbeesly running Invoke-Exfil to compress the Downloads directory into password-protected OfficeSupplies.7z (password 'lolol') and copy it to \\192.168.0.4\webdav using hardcoded credentials cozy/MyCozyPassw0rd!, i.e. collection/exfiltration using embedded credentials, consistent with T1552.001.

title: Get-PrivateKeys exports LocalMachine certificates to password-protected .pfx files on scranton
rationale: F27, F55 and F59 all describe the same action: pbeesly running Get-PrivateKeys from readme.ps1 to enumerate cert:\LocalMachine and export every certificate to random-named .pfx files (e.g. coyn5igj.3io.pfx) protected by hardcoded password 'saribas'. This is private-key/certificate theft, T1552.004.

title: Kerberos service-ticket requests for the krbtgt service with RC4 encryption
rationale: F47 describes three 4769 events requesting a krbtgt service ticket with RC4 encryption by pbeesly and SCRANTON$; unusual krbtgt service-ticket requests can accompany golden-ticket activity, best matching T1558.001, though no forged-ticket artifact was observed.

title: RC4-downgraded Kerberos service-ticket requests for machine accounts (Kerberoasting pattern)
rationale: F46 describes 28 Kerberos 4769 service-ticket requests with RC4-HMAC encryption for machine accounts NASHUA$, NEWYORK$, SCRANTON$, WEC$ by pbeesly@DMEVALS.LOCAL, the Kerberoasting pattern matching T1558.003.

title: PsExec-delivered python.exe lateral movement and C2 on nashua
rationale: Both findings describe the same action: PsExec64.exe with explicit credentials launching C:\Windows\Temp\python.exe on nashua (parent PSEXESVC.exe) with outbound TCP to 192.168.0.4:8443 and WebDAV retrieval of python.exe. This is credential-based lateral movement/remote execution, not credential access; best ATT&CK fit is T1021 (Remote Services).
